investigations.question: What changes in the foreground aisle around 18–30 s?
observed_evidence: A silver sedan changes position from the right side of the aisle toward the left across SNAP-020, SNAP-022 and SNAP-024; it is no longer in that position by SNAP-028.
A person in a dark top and light/tan trousers is visible at SNAP-018/020, moves toward the foreground/right by SNAP-022/024, and is partly occluded by the foreground red SUV in SNAP-026/028.
hypotheses_considered: The person and sedan pass near one another in the aisle.
discriminating_evidence_searched: Relative positions across the adaptive samples; visible separation/overlap and occlusion around the red SUV.
investigations.result: The person and sedan occupy nearby parts of the same aisle during the interval. No contact or directed interaction is established by the retained observations. Keep proximity as an observation, not an event claim.

investigations.question: Is the small blue object on the background access road persistent and moving?
observed_evidence: A blue vehicle-like form appears at changing locations on the background access road across SNAP-040/042/044/046/048/050.
It is no longer clearly visible by SNAP-054.
hypotheses_considered: A moving blue vehicle traverses the road.
A static object is revealed differently by tree occlusion.
discriminating_evidence_searched: Relative location against road bend, trees and fixed parking geometry across samples.
investigations.result: Position changes consistently with travel along the access road; precise vehicle type and complete path remain unresolved because of distance and tree occlusion.

investigations.question: What changes occur near the end of the segment?
observed_evidence: A white pickup is visible on the background road in the late samples and shifts leftward across the sampled interval.
A dark sedan appears in the foreground driving aisle around the late samples, changes position toward the left and remains visible at 105 s.
hypotheses_considered: Two separate vehicles are moving in distinct spatial regions.
The apparent changes might be from occlusion or sample differences.
discriminating_evidence_searched: Position relative to fixed road, parking-bay lines and parked vehicles across SNAP-094/095/097/098/100/102/104/105.
investigations.result: The vehicles occupy separate depth regions and show different trajectories. They are treated as distinct entities; exact entry/exit boundaries are not frame-accurately established.

investigations.question: Is the baseline inventory demonstrably complete for every visible semantic object?
observed_evidence: The baseline contains a dense parking area with many overlapping vehicles and several frame-edge crops.
The inventory records 45 visually separable vehicle instances from the t=0 scene, with location-based identifiers.
hypotheses_considered: All visually separable parked vehicles are represented.
One or more partly hidden/edge-cropped vehicles or small distant figures may be unresolved.
investigations.result: The 45-vehicle baseline is a manually enumerated inventory, not a detector-derived count. The dense overlap and cropped edges prevent a guarantee that every partially hidden or tiny distant object has been resolved. This limitation is explicit; do not treat the inventory as independently proven exhaustive.
